member.name: T:LibraryCompiler.Services.IBlobStore
member.summary: Read/write key→bytes storage that the host injects when it wants the compiler to persist artifacts across sessions. The compiler treats this strictly as an opaque blob store — it never asks where the bytes live, what filesystem is used, what quota applies, or how eviction is handled. Those are host concerns.

remarks.para:
Reference implementations live in the host (Kmila.Shared/Services/):
FileSystemBlobStore(rootPath) for desktop / dev tree.
MauiAppDataBlobStore for mobile (wraps FileSystem.AppDataDirectory).
IsolatedStorageBlobStore for sandboxed environments.
The lib ships and as portable defaults — useful for tests and for hosts that don't want any persistence at all.
Keys are caller-defined strings; the compiler uses content-hash keys for IEEE / user libraries so a different source produces a different key automatically (no mtime-based invalidation needed).
